composition.serve_who: This sheet illustrates the primary 24V DC Service Supply generation and distribution architecture. It details the conversion of 600V DC to 24V DC via PORT and STBD MAPS converters, the central +24V SERVICE BUS, its buffering by the AUX SERVICE BATTERY, and the primary high-current distribution feeders serving the FWD/AFT DC panels, Bilge Pump, and Fire Pump.

facts: The central +24V SERVICE BUS aggregates power from PORT MAPS (via SW1/SW2), STBD MAPS (via SW3/SW4), a 24V 110A AC-DC converter (via SW5), and the AUX SERVICE BAT. (via SW11 and Shunt #1).
It distributes heavy loads via fused branches: FWD DC PANEL (F5 100A, SW6), AFT DC PANEL (F6 200A, SW7), SO 6 / BILGE PUMP (F7 60A, SW8), SO 7 / FIRE PUMP (F8 60A, SW9), and SO 8 (F9 125A, SW10).

A central NEGATIVE BUS collects returns from the FWD/AFT DC PANELS, BILGE PUMP, FIRE PUMP, and battery banks (GEN START, EMERGENCY, AUX SERVICE), and ties directly to '230V AC GROUND (= SHIPS GROUND)'.
Isolators SW1 through SW5 are controlled via terminal strip T/S S and relays Re1/Re2. Relay Re2 coil is fed by the 'BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode)' (via Re 2a).
A dedicated 'PC CARD' acts as a control logic module, receiving status/command lines including NEG, BAE, AUX, and +EM, and interfacing with 'BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL' on pins 1-3.
The PORT 600V DC BUS supplies the PORT MAPS-1/2 converters via Q4 (32A) breakers.
The STBD 600V DC BUS supplies the STBD MAPS-1/2 converters via Q4 (32A) breakers.
The HVPDU buses are heavily protected upstream, shown with F1 and F2 500A fuses on the Port side before distributing to the breakers.
